root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers on the forepart of the head and its hair, especially the forelock. From grasping a person's or creature's forelock, the language also expresses control or mastery, with figurative extensions to leadership and distinction.
root_idea.development: The evidence records a development from the physical forelock to idiomatic authority and figurative prominence. Separate lexical branches include hair lengthening and a vegetation or pasture term.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The singular noun is the appropriate public dictionary headword.
This is the Quranic plural نَوَاصِي of the same noun, نَاصِيَة.

senses.definition: The hair growing at the front of the head; the forelock.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran in both singular and plural forms for the forelock or front hair.

senses.definition: Control or mastery expressed through taking or grasping someone or something by the forelock.
senses.usage_conditions: An idiomatic or metonymic construction in which holding the forelock signifies having power over the entity; explicitly applied to every creature in the Quranic expression from Hūd 11:56.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic specialization of the general forelock term; it is kept separate from the Quran-attested uses because the supplied Quran evidence does not specifically establish the horse-related application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The head or leading person of a people, by figurative extension from the forelock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression for prominence or leadership within a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stretch or extend someone's forelock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the cited expression concerning arranging or stretching a deceased person's forelock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For hair to grow or become long.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal use describing the lengthening of hair, distinct from the noun naming the forelock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vegetation term: a pasture regarded as among the best grazing grounds, also reported as a species of thistle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied descriptions do not settle the precise botanical referent; the pasture and thistle descriptions are retained within this vegetation branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The choice or best members of a people, by comparison with excellent pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative collective expression based on the evaluative sense of the pasture term.
